title: Introduce event-driven RAG 'saga' starter: durable tool-calling workflows and checkpointing
author: Lina Park
commits: scaffold: add rag-saga starter structure and runner
feat(ts): implement ts saga runner, example tools and README
feat(py): add python shim and durable checkpoint adapter
docs: add RAG Saga quickstart page and diagrams
ci: add smoke e2e job for rag-saga examples
description:
Motivation: Teams building multi-step RAG flows often need durable, observable orchestrations where tool-calls, retrieval steps, and LLM responses form a recoverable transaction. This PR introduces a lightweight "saga" starter that demonstrates an event-driven, checkpointed approach for RAG sessions so developers can build fault-tolerant tool-calling agents without having to run a heavy workflow engine.

Summary: Adds an examples/rag-saga folder with TypeScript and Python variants of a saga runner, a set of small example tools (search, fetch-metadata, synthesize-summary), and a durable checkpoint adapter that persists step events and KV state to Redis (pluggable, with notes for Dynamo/Firestore). The package includes: a step-by-step quickstart doc (docs/quickstarts/rag-saga.md), a local devcontainer for playing with the example, and a CI smoke job to validate basic flows. The saga pattern used here intentionally keeps control flow simple: linear steps with compensations and idempotent tool-call wrappers (no external workflow runtime required).

What is included (developer-facing):
- TypeScript starter: examples/rag-saga/ts with saga-runner.ts, basic tools, and a README showing a 5-minute walk-through.
- Python shim: examples/rag-saga/py to show how platform clients can interop with existing Python workers.
- Durable adapter: a pluggable persistence adapter that checkpoints "events" and last-known KV so processes can restart mid-session. Redis example implementation included and documented.
- Observability hooks: the runner emits structured traces (span names) and lightweight telemetry counters compatible with Redwood Console ingestion (examples show tag usage: session_id, step_name, model_variant).
- Quickstart doc: docs/quickstarts/rag-saga.md includes architecture diagram, local setup, and migration notes for teams currently using ephemeral in-memory sessions.

Backward compatibility and safety: This is only an examples repo change and adds no runtime code to hosted or dedicated serving. The pattern avoids blocking on long-running network calls; tool-calls are executed as separate processes or tasks and results are posted back to the saga via event append. The starter emphasizes idempotency and provides helper utilities to make tool functions retry-safe.

Testing and verification:
- Local: devcontainer includes Redis and a shell script to run both TS and PY examples end-to-end.
- CI: smoke job runs the TS example with Node 18 and the python shim under 3.11; e2e assertions validate final summary tokens and that checkpoints were written and read.

Checklist:
- [x] Example runner + tools for TypeScript
- [x] Python shim and adapter example
- [x] Quickstart docs and architecture diagram
- [x] Devcontainer and local run script
- [x] CI smoke job
- [x] Observability and tagging examples for Redwood Console

How to use: Follow docs/quickstarts/rag-saga.md for local dev. High level: run Redis, start TS runner, exercise the example HTTP tool endpoints, simulate a crash (kill process) and restart runner to confirm checkpoint replay and resume from last completed step. The README includes curl examples and a small test harness for reproducible behavior.

Notes for reviewers:
- The Redis adapter is intentionally minimal; comment if you'd prefer we add a second adapter implementation (Dynamo/Firestore) in this PR or follow-up.
- I added tracing hooks that mirror our internal conventions; open to renaming spans/tags to match Console onboarding guidance.

Related work: ENG-9812 (durable-session patterns), PM-221 (quickstart for robust agents), SUP-4832 (customer request for resuming partial RAG sessions after transient failures).

Release notes: Adds an examples quickstart demonstrating a durable event-driven RAG orchestration pattern with TypeScript and Python samples. Suitable for workshops and internal demos.

Security: No secrets are checked in. Devcontainer uses ephemeral Redis with no auth for local dev; docs call out KMS/secret-manager patterns for production adapters.
